Seminar Title:

Sustainable Photocatalytic Degradation of Dyes and Textile Wastewater using Non-metal Doped g-C3N4-based Catalyst

Seminar Type:

Synopsis Seminar

Department:

Civil Engineering

Speaker Name:

Subhalaxmi Sahoo ( Rollno : 521ce1004)

Speaker Type:

Student

Venue:

Seminar Hall, Department of Civil Engineering

Date and Time:

30 Sep 2026 10.30 am

Contact:

Prateeksha Mahamallik

Abstract:

Photocatalysis among various advanced oxidation processes (AOPs) is one of the efficient methods to degrade and mineralize the chemically complex dye molecule and produce intermediate and toxic free end products. Graphitic carbon nitride (g-C3N4) is an environmentally friendly potent metal-free photocatalyst because it works under visible light, is inexpensive, and is easy to prepare. In the present study, we have synthesized different photocatalytic material such as oxygen-doped g-C3N4 (OCN), surfur and chlorine doped g-C3N4 (S,Cl-CN), and chitosan S,Cl-CN composite (CS/S,Cl-CN) beads to degrade various synthetic and real textile wastewater (RTW). The prepared catalysts have been characterized by XRD, FTIR, FESEM, EDX, DRS, PL, pHzpc analyses. Methylene blue (MB) is degraded under natural sunlight using OCN. The decolourization efficiencies are measures for different parametric variation studies. The degradation follows the first-order kinetics under different operational conditions. A cradle-to-gate life cycle assessment (LCA) study has been conducted to determine the environmental impact of the photocatalytic process. The end-point results of the LCA study confirms a negative impact on human health (0.00027 disability-adjusted life years), ecosystem quality (26.74 PDF&middotm2&middotyear), and climate change (207.88 kg CO2), and resource depletion (3,060.82 MJ) was mainly driven by the use of urea and electricity in the process.

S,Cl-CN catalyst has been used to degrade binary dye (BD) having MB and crystal violet (CV) under LED light irradiation in the presence of H2O2. In addition, the catalyst has been successfully applied for the degradation of real textile wastewater from the dyeing stage. The eco-toxicity assessment of the process has been performed through the germination and growth of green gram seed in the treated water, which confirms the environmental safety and low toxicity of the process. Response Surface Methodology (RSM) and Artificial Neural Networks (ANN) have been applied to establish the interaction between the independent variables and BD decolourization, and finally the process is optimized. The efficiency of real wastewater decolourization is 46.11% in 180 minutes with S,Cl-CN dose 2.5 g/L, and 611.81 mM H2O2 concentration. COD removal of 40.07% has been found with 5 g/L S,Cl-CN dose, and 611.81 mM of H2O2 concentration within 180 minutes.
Decolourization of MB and RTW have been explored by photocatalytic degradation using CS/S,Cl-CN beads in batch and continuous reactor, respectively. The parametric effects on RTW decolourization and COD removal of the RTW in a continuous reactor has been studied.
